# Set up a new vault

Read directly for this operation: [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), [operations](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md).
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

Initialize the wiki vault.

1. Verify this is the intended new vault root. Open an operation before
   scaffolding, using the fresh-vault exception in the completion contract.
   Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/init.mjs"`.
2. Verify the expected folders, schema, templates and catalog exist. Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"`; it checks files without
   requiring a running app. Log and close the operation; sync only if authorized
   and configured. Report a non-git vault as local-only.
3. Relay the one-time app setup steps (open the folder as a vault, verify with
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" vaults`, import the Web Clipper template). Report app registration
   separately from completed filesystem initialization; do not claim a health
   report proved the CLI can reach Obsidian.

skills/wiki-maintainer/references/access.content:
# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
After an unavailable CLI or timeout, choose the supported fallback once; never
loop waiting for the app. **A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome.** Read
the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.
OS cleanup releases a lock after process death, but cannot prove a surviving CLI
child or an already-submitted Obsidian mutation finished. Inspect uncertain targets.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

On Windows, use PowerShell or the Node wrapper for Obsidian; Git Bash can select
the GUI executable instead of `Obsidian.com` and return misleading empty output.
These reporting examples are read-only: do not open an operation or rebuild the
index merely to answer a question.

# Keeping knowledge findable and trustworthy

Use this contract when creating concepts, linking topics, discovering sources or reviewing answers. The schema stays small; explanatory prose supplies the nuance.

## Concept identity

Before creating a concept, search its intended title, common alternative wording, and the nearest existing concepts. Choose explicitly: extend the canonical page, add an equivalent alias, or create a distinct concept with a scope boundary. Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/identity-audit.mjs" --json` from the plugin root when ambiguity is suspected. Never merge based on embedding similarity alone.

Use `aliases: ["equivalent phrase"]` and a one-sentence `scope:` on concept pages. Aliases name the same concept; broader, narrower and complementary concepts remain separate pages. Use full-path wikilinks for ambiguous names. A source page and a concept may legitimately share a basename; a warning is a review queue, not permission to rename everything.

## Relationships and citations

Keep citations in `sources:` and in the prose they support. Citation targets point to `wiki/sources/` or `raw/`, using full paths when needed. A source page must identify its own raw clipping. Reachable evidence establishes a citation route, not that a claim is true or entailed by it.

Put navigation in `## Relationships` or `Related:`. Use a small role vocabulary: **broader**, **narrower**, **prerequisite**, **complements**, **alternative**, **contrasts**, **applies-to**. Each link needs a sentence explaining the relationship and its limits. For example: `Complements [[wiki/concepts/Intention-Action Gap.md|Intention–Action Gap]]: this intervention addresses a gap between intending and acting under the conditions described above.` Do not turn similar wording into a causal claim. Clearly label cross-source interpretations as synthesis; retain their supporting citations outside the navigation section.

Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/relationships.mjs" --limit=10 --json` to generate candidates. Shared sources and semantic neighbors are reasons to inspect, never proof of a relationship. Review both pages and their evidence; accept only links with a useful explanation. Reuse existing user authorization for the requested relink scope. Do not grow links merely to improve a graph score.

## Task maps and discovery

Curated `moc/` maps answer a recurring task: where to start, prerequisites, competing approaches, complementary domains, and unresolved questions. Keep generated project catalogs as a section or separate linked page. Search indexes both wiki pages and MOCs. Maintain a few useful maps instead of a universal taxonomy.

Discovery starts with an unanswered question and bounded search of the existing wiki/MOCs. Each candidate source must state what evidence it adds and which existing or proposed concept/synthesis it changes. Deduplicate source URLs as before. Read the manual Start here section of `index.md` only if needed; never load its generated catalog as the default coverage summary. Promote high-use stubs and missing bridges when their current evidence is sufficient; do not pad stubs or enforce a source:synthesis ratio.

## Verification and maintenance cadence

- **Each ingest or substantive edit:** check identity and citation paths, update the affected task map, refresh the index through the operation helper. Update `updated` for edits; set `reviewed` only after checking factual claims against evidence or project behavior.
- **Each requested maintenance pass:** inspect structural defects, then sample changed/high-use pages even if the structural score is perfect. Run drift coverage first; choose a bounded sample for embeddings and claim inspection. Record evaluated, skipped and failed counts, plus document/chunk sampling coverage. Long documents are sampled; a page counted as evaluated is not an exhaustive factual review.
- **Weekly when actively growing:** review up to ten relationship candidates, high-demand stubs and discovery gaps. This is a workflow cadence, not an installed scheduler.
- **After search/schema changes and periodically as vocabulary evolves:** run the retrieval regression set, inspect development failures, then measure held-out queries without tuning to them. Keep results by category rather than one misleading health score.

`reviewed` means factual verification; `updated` means edited; search index freshness means the indexed file version matches the file. None substitutes for the others. Missing review dates remain unverified. Cosine drift is a topical diagnostic, not a truth or contradiction detector. A zero-evaluated run cannot justify saying the wiki has no drift.

Read [wiki efficacy](../../../docs/wiki-efficacy.md) for command contracts and evaluation examples.

skills/wiki-maintainer/references/eviden.content:
# Evidence and editorial policy

## Page schema and dates

Wiki frontmatter declares `type` (source/entity/concept/synthesis/authored),
`created`, `updated`, `reviewed`, `status` (stub/draft/maintained), `sources` and
honest `ai-generated` authorship. Follow the vault's schema; missing `reviewed`
means unverified, never substitute `updated`. Keep three dates distinct:
`updated` means edited, `reviewed` means claims checked against evidence or current
project behavior, and index freshness means indexed content matches the files.
Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.

Use exact citation paths and `[[wikilinks]]`; `![[embeds]]` are transclusion, not
relationship edges. Write unwrapped logical lines and never split a wikilink over
a line break. Use [identity and relationships](efficacy.md) for concept reuse and
explained links. Original documentation follows
[authoring](../../wiki-user/references/authoring.md).

## Non-negotiable guardrails
1. **`raw/` bodies are immutable.** Read raw sources; never edit their content —
   it is the evidence every wiki page cites. Frontmatter is pipeline state and
   may be updated by wiki-master tooling only.
   Only clipping tools create raw evidence; never move it to record ingestion
   state. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it.
2. **Provenance on every claim.** Each wiki page you write carries `sources: ["[[...]]"]`
   linking back to the `raw/` notes it derives from, plus `ai-generated: true`.
   **Exception: `wiki/authored/`** — original content with no `raw/` counterpart
   (advisory documentation, policy, house style) declares this explicitly via
   `sources: []`, never by omission. `ai-generated` still records actual
   authorship (`true` if you drafted it, `false` if the human did) — the
   disclosure is about provenance, not about who wrote the words.
3. **Cite when you answer.** Query answers reference the pages/sources they rest on.
4. **Flag, don't invent.** If sources contradict or are silent, say so — never
   paper over a gap with plausible text.
5. **Clippings win.** Briefs, discovery summaries, corrections files, and your
   own memory of a source are *claims, not authority*: verify every quote,
   figure, and attribution against the clipping in `raw/` before it lands on a
   page, and when they disagree the clipping prevails — including when the
   instruction is the user's. Every layer between the source and the page is a
   lossy compressor whose errors read exactly like facts; authority flows
   outward from the one artifact that cannot drift.
   Scope edges, which matter as much as the rule:
   - It guarantees **fidelity, not truth** — a faithful clipping of a wrong page
     is still wrong; quality tiers and cross-clipping corroboration handle
     credibility.
   - A **degraded capture** (bad OCR, partial extraction) wins as evidence of
     what the vault *holds*, not of what the author typed — don't trust it at
     character level.
   - A clipping's **silence proves "not supported here," never "false"** —
     record unsourced claims as unsourced (visibly, on the page) rather than
     asserting or deleting them. The vault cannot cite what it does not hold.

## Reddit and Medium

Reddit posts and comments, and articles on medium.com or its subdomains, are
eligible sources. Keep their material in separate labeled sections in every
derived page and query answer: `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` for Reddit
and `## Medium articles` for Medium. Put platform-derived claims, quotes,
reported experiences and any inference that relies on them in the corresponding
section; do not blend the two platforms together or with higher-quality evidence.
This applies to source summaries, concepts, entities and syntheses, including
material reused through another wiki page. Even a summary of a single platform
source needs its heading. Raw clippings retain the captured content without rewriting.

Attribute statements to their authors and cite the captured evidence. For Reddit,
do not turn a few comments into consensus, prevalence or established facts.
Disclose missing comments or reply context when the capture is incomplete;
do not claim a full thread was captured without verifying it. Upvotes do not
establish credibility.

Keep Reddit and Medium citations and dependent conclusions out of the main factual
sections, opening summary and recommendations. A fact independently supported
by higher-quality evidence may appear there with those independent citations;
any platform comparison stays in its labeled section. Retain all provenance in
`sources:` frontmatter. Assess individual sources using the existing credibility
rubric; allowing capture does not automatically upgrade their credibility.
Official platform documentation and policy pages outside discussion threads or
Medium articles do not require these labels.

## Style: viewpoints whole, conclusions after, breadcrumbs always
Narrative is licensed; dismissal is not. Three house rules govern every page:

1. **Opposing viewpoints appear in their entirety** — in their own strongest
   terms, attributed to their holders — before any conclusion engages them.
   A viewpoint the page ends up arguing against gets the same care as one it
   endorses; weight follows the evidence the vault holds, and no viewpoint is
   waved off by tone (loaded verbs, scare quotes, "supposedly"). When sources
   conflict, keep the claims separate and attributed — never resolve them into
   one synthesized voice that erases the disagreement.
2. **Viewpoints first, conclusions after — and conclusions declare themselves.**
   Every analytic sentence is one of: *inherited* (a source says it — cite it),
   *extended* (built on a source — cite it, mark what's added), or *original*
   (the wiki's own inference — say so explicitly, never state it in the
   page's neutral voice). Joining source A to source B to imply C is an
   *original* claim even when A and B are both cited.
3. **The breadcrumb trail is non-negotiable.** Every viewpoint and every
   conclusion must be walkable back to `raw/`: `sources:` frontmatter, inline
   `[[wikilinks]]` to the source pages, and quotes verified per guardrail #5.
   A conclusion whose trail dead-ends is a defect, however good it reads.

Per-type licenses (neutrality is a property of a page type, not of the vault):
- `raw/` — fidelity only; the evidence layer (guardrail #1, #5).
- `wiki/entities/` — **describe and only describe.** Convert opinions to
  attributed facts about who holds them; convert evaluations to the measurable
  facts beneath them. When tempted to interpret, link to a concept or
  synthesis instead.
- `wiki/concepts/` — claims with grounding. Assertive titles are allowed; the
  title's pressure is the point, and the body must support the claim under
  rules 1–3.
- `wiki/syntheses/` — the licensed narrative layer: weigh, judge, conclude —
  bounded by rules 1–3, and labeled as the wiki's synthesis.
- `wiki/authored/` — the vault's own first-party voice: advisory documentation,
  policy, house style, or other original work with no `raw/` evidence behind it
  by design. Same full narrative license as syntheses; state recommendations
  directly. Rule 3 (breadcrumb to `raw/`) does not apply — there is deliberately
  nothing to trail, declared via `sources: []` rather than left silent.

Clippings carry `quality: high|medium|low`, an AI credibility rating. Treat low-quality sources with extra skepticism during ingestion; lint may flag claims supported only by low-quality provenance. Capture fidelity and source credibility are separate judgments.

`citation-status: quarantined` is an explicit do-not-cite restriction, independent of credibility and character fidelity. Do not use that capture as supporting evidence or repeat dependent claims without independent support. Citing pages may carry `citation-status: restricted` and a warning identifying the affected evidence. A different state, `citation-status: retired`, marks a note that is a lead and must not be cited as support: `health` does not ask it for evidence and reports any page that cites it (`cites-retired-page`). Do not use `retired` for a page that merely leans on a quarantined clipping; that is `restricted`, and it stays under the evidence check. Preserve the restriction when reusing summaries; removing an item from triage is not permission to cite it. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md).

HTML clips may also carry `fidelity: partial` and `fidelity-checks: <count>`. The clipper compares recognized source headings, callouts, availability notices, API introductions and feature-list items with extracted text, plus whole normalized endpoint summaries and parameter rows, and literal supplied code examples in recognized REST layouts. Missing probes queue fidelity triage. `fidelity-ignored: <count>` records headings set aside as site chrome (a feedback widget, a sidebar); they open no triage, and their labels are printed when the clip is made. Inspect the triage issues before quoting affected material. Zero warnings is not proof of completeness: unrecognized structures, unselected UI tabs and content absent from supplied HTML are outside this check. See [HTML clipping fidelity](../../../docs/clipping-fidelity.md).

A URL can have more than one capture. A recapture (`clip.mjs <url> --recapture`) is a second, dated clipping of the same page, written beside the first: its name and `title` end ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, its `created` is the day it was made, and `recapture-of` names the newest capture it follows, as a vault path. The older clipping is never edited, so both are evidence of what the page said on their own dates, each with its own `source-hash`; cite the capture whose text you quote. The ingest backlog treats two captures with different text as two sources. `extraction: manual` marks a page a person saved from a signed-in browser and supplied with `clip.mjs <url> --from-file <path>`: `source` is the page's real address, nothing was fetched, `supplied-sha256` is the hash of the supplied bytes (the file's name is not recorded) and `source-hash` that of the stored text. Like `ocr` and `rendered`, it names how the text was obtained and is not a defect. `apply-reclips` refuses such a clipping, because a fetched page would replace the supplied text; refresh it with `clip.mjs <url> --from-file <path> --recapture`. The clipper still refuses a supplied login, consent or age-gate page and a supplied page under 100 words. See [recapture, saved pages and the decline and known-URL commands](../../../docs/clipping-fidelity.md#recapture-saved-pages-and-the-decline-and-known-url-commands-0870).

# Report wiki health and backlog

Read directly for this operation: [access](access.md), [maintenance](maintenance.md).
This entry point is read-only; do not open an operation, write a log, or refresh the index.

Run the deterministic health check and report the result to the user.

Steps:
1. Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` using the absolute installed path.
2. Present `Open integrity defects` with scanned-page coverage. For issue IDs,
   locations, evidence and verification conditions, run the same helper with
   `--json`. Distinguish unscored forward links from defects; age and similarity
   do not prove an accidental break. An empty scan is not a healthy-wiki verdict.
3. Use `--backlog` for ingest reporting. The old capped score and topology counts
   are available with `--legacy` for historical comparison only; do not use them
   as a repair target. Zero integrity defects does not establish factual accuracy.
4. Route authorized repair work to [maintainer repair](repair.md).
   Do not modify any files in this reporting skill.

skills/wiki-maintainer/references/lint.m.content:
# Review wiki consistency and factual claims

Read [access and host commands](access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](evidence.md), [efficacy](efficacy.md), [operations](operations.md).
Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [maintenance](maintenance.md) when a structural repair, migration or backfill is actually indicated.
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

1. Run maintainer health first: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"`. Stop for an empty
   wiki. A clean graph does not skip semantic review: sample changed or high-use
   pages for stale claims, contradictory evidence and missing useful connections.
   Route structural integrity findings to [maintainer repair](repair.md)
   within the authorized scope; keep unresolved navigation outside defect counts.
   Keep the sample bounded and report its size. Open an operation only before
   making edits:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op lint` — records what was already
   uncommitted, so step 6 commits your fixes and not the user's in-progress work.
2. Run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/drift.mjs" --coverage`, then a bounded embedding check:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/drift.mjs" --limit=10`. Read eligible/evaluated/failed/skipped
   counts. Zero evaluated is not a clean result; report missing evidence or backend
   failures. Similarity is a topical diagnostic, never proof of claim correctness.
3. Run the content lint: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lint.mjs"` (warn-only,
   never scored; `--json` for the full list, `--tier=convention|gapped|unverified`,
   `--page=<substr>`, `--full` for untruncated quotes). It sorts each quote the
   verbatim check cannot place into a tier and leads with the counts. How quotation
   marks pair (curly marks nest, straight marks alternate) and which spans the style
   flags skip are in the [content lint contract](../../../README.md#content-lint):
   - **convention** — the evidence has the same words in the same order; markup,
     punctuation or extraction spacing differ. Counted, not listed; leave it unless
     the count jumps.
   - **gapped** — every quoted word is in the evidence in order, with extra evidence
     words between them, which are listed. A header, timestamp or citation is
     extraction noise. A dropped clause or two joined sentences is a silent omission:
     restore the words or add an ellipsis. Read each inserted run.
   - **unverified** — a word is changed, added, reordered or negated (so is a dropped
     negation or operator), or the page's evidence trail does not hold the text.
     `--near` prints, for unverified quotes of six or more words that align with a
     raw clipping at 0.85 or better, a word diff (`[-word-]` the page added,
     `{+word+}` only the clipping has): read those first. Each is a quotation with a
     small difference; a corrected typo is benign, a changed meaning is not. A quote
     it does not list is usually the page's own wording, but a low score is no proof.
     Adjudicate a bounded sample and report its size: real drift gets fixed against
     the clipping (guardrail #5); the wiki's own wording, mention quotes and
     retracted claims are conventions to ignore; claims the vault genuinely doesn't
     hold get marked unsourced on the page. Confirm the trail itself resolves (an
     ambiguous or misrouted citation) before editing a quote. Two-column captures
     with interleaved text land here too.
   Scope the run to the work: `--updated-since=<YYYY-MM-DD>` for the pages edited
   since a date, `--paths-file=<ledger>` for the pages a task wrote (both may be
   given). The graph is still built whole, so a scoped run saves the quote checks,
   not the initial graph scan. Record what you read, so the next run does not
   list it again: `lint.mjs --ids` shows each finding's id, then
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/lint-disposition.mjs" record --ids=<id>,<id>
   --disposition=own-wording|mention|title|markup|accepted --reviewer=<name>
   (--page=<path> | --paths-file=<ledger> | --whole-vault)`. Use `fixed` only for a
   quote you corrected (a finding still present after `fixed` is listed again). The
   verdicts are lines in `lint-dispositions.jsonl` at the vault root; add that file
   to the operation's ledger. A changed quote or a replaced clipping is a new
   finding and needs a new reading. `--include-reviewed` lists the reviewed ones.
   Style flags per the v0.2.2 licenses are pointers for review, not violations.
4. Read the flagged pages (orphans, hub-stubs, drifted). Look for: contradictions
   between pages, claims superseded by newer sources, concepts referenced but
   unwritten, and missing cross-references.
5. Apply only safe, unambiguous fixes; present the rest as a proposed change list
   for the user to approve when not already authorized. Set `updated` on edited
   pages; stamp `reviewed` only where claims were actually verified against their
   evidence or current project behavior. Mechanical links, aliases and formatting
   preserve prior `reviewed` dates. Record what was checked and what remains
   uncertain. If no edits are applied, return the report without a log or operation.
   For applied fixes, validate links and refresh affected catalogs; write the log entry:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op lint --title "<summary>"` (details on stdin).
6. Close the operation:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op lint --title "<summary>" --since <saved-token>`
   (An `op-commit` with no `--paths-file` is refused while any other operation is open; scope it with `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>` and `--paths-file <ledger>`.)
   A lint that applied fixes and did not commit them leaves the vault changed with
   no record — the failure `/wiki-purge` was built to end. The helper does not push; push and verify remote publication through the shared contract.

skills/wiki-maintainer/references/mainte.content:
# Maintenance metrics, repairs and limits

## Integrity worklist

`health.mjs` now leads with the uncapped open integrity defect count. Use `--json`
for versioned issues with stable IDs, exact locations, evidence and verification
conditions. Intentional forward links, orphan/dead-end opportunities and stubs do
not increase that count. A required citation that fails remains a defect even on
a stub. Original authored pages may declare `sources: []`; substantive derived
pages still require evidence. Unresolved navigation, age and fuzzy suggestions
are never proof of an accidental break. The old capped score is available only
through `--legacy`, for historical/topology reporting rather than repair targets.

Use [maintainer repair](repair.md) for authorized integrity repairs.
Compare resolved, remaining and new issue IDs after each batch. `--backlog` keeps
the ingest contract below. The checker is structural and reports its unchecked
areas; zero defects is not factual verification. See `docs/wiki-integrity.md` in
the plugin root for the full contract and coverage limits.

## "Has this been ingested?" — a content-hash join, not a guess
A raw clipping is **ingested iff its `source-hash` is recorded in some
`wiki/sources/` page's `source-hashes`**. Hash equality is the contract — immune to
the `-<hash7>` filename suffix and the citation-format drift that made
link-resolution manufacture phantom backlog. Facts the metric reports:

| metric | means | still owes work? |
|---|---|---|
| `unparsedSources` | nothing in the wiki cites it at all | yes |
| `unsummarizedSources` | no `wiki/sources` page records its hash | **yes — this is the backlog** |
| `missingHash` | a `.md` clipping carrying no `source-hash` | data defect — repair (re-clip) |
| `backfillPending` | source pages that cite raw but recorded no hash | migrate — see the migration guidance in this reference |
| `provenanceGaps` | a `wiki/sources` page citing no `raw/` file | yes — scored as a defect |

Report `unsummarizedSources` when asked what still needs ingesting — obtain it
with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`, which prints just these ingest lines led
by the not-ingested count (the full `health.mjs` report carries the same lines at
the bottom). Do **not** re-derive the backlog by searching `tag:clippings` and
hand-diffing `wiki/sources/` — that fuzzy link-resolution is the drift this
content-hash join exists to replace. Only `.md`
clippings are ingestable units — a binary original (`.pdf/.xlsx/.zip`) is never a
summary target and is not backlog.

**Migrating a vault (agents, any machine).** A vault written before this scheme has
source pages without `source-hashes`; a transitional fallback keeps them credited by
link resolution so nothing regresses, but `backfillPending > 0` means the migration
has not run here. Repair it from the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backfill-source-hashes.mjs"`
(dry-run) then `--apply`. It is idempotent and guesses nothing — ambiguous/unresolved
citations are logged for review. If the vault is git-synced, running it once and
committing repairs every machine.

**Repairing title-shaped citations (`provenanceGaps > 0`).** A separate, older drift:
ingest wrote `sources: ["[[<the source's title>]]"]`, but the clipper had already
slugified that title into the filename (`/`, `:`, `#` → `-`, 120-char cap). Any title
carrying one of those characters or running long cites a file that does not exist —
the page is a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, though the ingest
was correct. Repair from the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"`
(dry-run) then `--apply`. It joins on `source-hash`, never on the title (the title is
what drifted), and reports anything it cannot pin to exactly one clipping instead of
guessing. Always cite a clipping by its **path**, `[[raw/clippings/<file>.md]]`.

**Repairing hard-wrapped wikilinks (`health.mjs` defects marked "hard-wrapped
wikilink").** Hand- or LLM-authored prose that gets word-wrapped at some column width
can break a `[[Target]]` straddling the wrap point into `[[Target\ncontinued]]` —
Obsidian wikilinks cannot span a line break, so this can never resolve and is always a
defect, never a healthy deferred forward-link (`classifyBrokenLinks` never lets a
wrapped target hide there, whether or not a suggestion resolves). **Prevention that
actually holds**: write vault content as unwrapped logical lines — never hard-wrap a
paragraph, and never let one contain a `[[wikilink]]` split across a line break — the
same discipline `clip-docx`'s `--wrap=none` already enforces mechanically on the docx
path. A written reminder alone is not the safeguard: maintainer relink's own `op-commit`
step reports any wrapped link introduced by the files it just committed, and
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` always scores one as a defect, so either catches a recurrence
even if the writing habit doesn't. Repair existing ones from the plugin root:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-wrapped-links.mjs"` (dry-run) then `--apply`. The fix is a lossless
whitespace-collapse (undoing the wrap, never guessing content); the one shape it cannot
safely resolve alone — a hyphen glued to the word right before the break, e.g.
`[[Diagno-\nstics]]`, indistinguishable by character shape from a title that
legitimately ends a line in a trailing hyphen (`[[Wizards-\n  Definition...]]`, a real
title) — is checked against the real page index (not edit-distance guessing) and only
fixed when exactly one reading resolves; left untouched and reported otherwise. See
`scripts/lib/dewrap-links.mjs`.

**Repairing invalid `sources:`/`source-hashes:` ordering.** A now-fixed bug in
`insertSourceHashes` could insert `source-hashes:` between a block-list `sources:`
key and its own `- [[...]]` item instead of after it — invalid YAML that a real
parser rejects outright, so Obsidian reports "No frontmatter found" on the page
(every property, not just `sources`) even though wiki-master's own regex-based
scripts tolerate it and never flagged it as a defect. Repair from the plugin root:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-sources-order.mjs"` (dry-run) then `--apply`. Pure string
surgery — it recognizes and reorders only that exact shape and is a no-op on
anything else — idempotent and safe to re-run.

**Repairing ambiguous bare links.** A bare `[[architecture]]` is an `ambiguous-link` defect when two pages
share the name. From the plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-ambiguous-links.mjs"` (dry
run, with the plan and the report) then `--apply`; `--project=<slug>` bounds it. On its own it applies one rule:
the page lives in a project's folder (`wiki/authored/<project>/`) and exactly one candidate does too, so the
link is rewritten to that path with the displayed text kept (`[[wiki/authored/<project>/architecture.md|architecture]]`;
`\|` inside a table row; an existing alias or `#heading` kept; a `sources:` entry takes the full path with no
alias). Links in code, comments and a generated catalog fence stay. Every other class is reported with its
reason, not guessed: a page outside every project folder (`shared-page`), several candidates or none in the
page's project (`needs-reading`), a title shared by two clippings (`title-citation`, repaired by retitling the
clippings, not from the citing page), an occurrence only inside a generated catalog (`catalog-line`, repaired by
regenerating it). A reviewed `--mapping=<file>` of `{ "target", "path", "page"? }` settles the ones that need a
reading, and only with a path that is a candidate. A page an application reads by title, where a path in a
citation would break it, is left alone with `--exclude=<path-prefix>` (repeatable). It sets `updated` to the run
date, leaves `reviewed`, and checks line by line that only wikilinks changed.

**Renaming clippings that Obsidian hides or a wikilink cannot carry.** Obsidian does
not index a dot-prefixed file, and `graph.mjs` skips the same names, so a clipping
filed as `.github-workflows-build.yml.md` is invisible: every citation of it is an
`unresolved-citation`, and an uncited one never reaches the ingest backlog. A backtick
in a filename is the same trap in another form (a backtick pair inside a wikilink reads
as a code span). The clippers now write `dot-github-workflows-build.yml.md` and drop
backticks (`scripts/lib/clip-names.mjs`); a re-clip of `clip-gh` adopts a file written
under its old name instead of copying it or, in digest mode, pruning it. Rename the
existing ones from the plugin root:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/rename-unsafe-clippings.mjs"` (dry-run), then
`--apply --paths-out <ledger.json>` inside an operation and close with
`op-commit --paths-file <ledger.json>`; the ledger lists the old names, the new names and
the pages rewritten. It renames only `.md` files under `raw/` (a state file such as
`raw/book-nom/.booknom-state.json` is hidden on purpose), leaves clipping content and
therefore `source-hash` alone, repoints full-path wikilinks in every page except `raw/`,
`log/` and `_templates/` (a link in a code block is an example and stays), reports other
mentions of an old path without rewriting them, and refuses a rename whose target exists.
Pages are rewritten before files are renamed, so an interrupted run is finished by running
it again.

**Renaming clippings whose names double the extension.** Before 0.58.0 a clipping of
`README.md` was filed `README.md.md`, and a title-less raw document `SKILL.md.md`; new clippings
no longer end `.md.md`. Rename the existing ones from the plugin root with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/rename-doubled-extension-clippings.mjs" --list-out <review.tsv>`
(dry run, writes nothing to the vault), review the listing, then `--apply --paths-out <ledger.json>`
inside an operation and close with `op-commit --paths-file <ledger.json>`. A `clip-gh` file
under `raw/clippings/gh/<owner>/<repo>/` loses its second `.md`; a top-level clipping with an empty
title is renamed from its source URL, nearest folder first, as new clips are. The contract is
the one above (bytes and `source-hash` untouched, full-path wikilinks only, `raw/` and `log/`
never rewritten, a rename onto an existing name refused), plus three more. A link to the
extension-stripped path is repointed only when no existing file has exactly that path (a vault
may hold both `Build.md` and `build.md.md`; a link to `Build.md` means the real file). The apply
refuses to start when any file it would change has uncommitted changes in the vault's git, because
another writer may be editing it, and changes nothing. `--flag=<prefix>` lists the pages under a prefix
for review and `--exclude=<prefix>` reports them without rewriting (both repeatable): use them for pages
whose citations an app reads by title. A bare-name link such as `[[README.md]]` is not rewritten.

**Backfilling `project:`/`kind:` onto pre-existing `wiki/authored/` pages.** A vault
whose authored pages predate this convention has none of it set. Repair from the
plugin root: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backfill-authored-metadata.mjs"` (dry-run) then `--apply`
— deterministic, filename- and content-shape-driven classification (never a guess:
a field it cannot resolve confidently is left unset rather than labeled wrong), and
idempotent, so it is safe to re-run as new authored pages arrive without metadata
of their own yet.

**Never move files to record ingestion state.** `raw/` immutability is the
load-bearing invariant. The hash key lives *in* the markdown — each page's
`source-hashes`, co-located with the summary that owns it — a single source of truth
that merges cleanly across machines. Derive the backlog at read time from that key,
like `index.md`; never copy ingestion state into the filesystem layout, where it can
drift and where two concurrent sessions race on the move.

## Known limits of the pattern
Stated so they are not rediscovered as surprises. The pattern this vault
implements bounds itself in ways worth tracking:
- **Index-only navigation is untested past the scale the source reports.** The
  source pattern says it "works surprisingly well at moderate scale (~100 sources,
  ~hundreds of pages)" — a claim about where it works, **not a ceiling**. It names
  no threshold and no failure mode. Separately, under an *Optional* heading, it
  says "as the wiki grows you want proper search" and suggests `qmd`, attaching no
  number; the two passages are not joined in the source, so do not present ~100 as
  the trigger for adopting search tooling. What is fair to say: a vault far past
  that figure is outside the range the source reports, entry may have shifted from
  reading `index.md` to `obsidian search` without anyone noticing, and **nobody has
  measured whether that costs anything**. Say that, and say it is untested — do not
  upgrade it into a bound the source never stated.
- **Cheap maintenance is not correct maintenance.** The pattern's justification is
  that upkeep cost approaches zero, which addresses effort, not accuracy. It
  specifies no verification tier — that is what maintainer lint, quote-lint, and the
  clipping-wins guardrail exist to supply.
- **Frictionless collection is not free.** Automated discovery plus automated
  ingest removes the cost that used to limit what got kept. Volume is not
  progress; prefer fewer, better-corroborated sources over a larger pile.

## Cost discipline
During substantive maintenance, cheap structural checks (maintainer health)
prioritize the expensive semantic passes. A clean graph does not establish factual correctness:
sample changed or high-use pages during requested maintenance even when structural
health is clean. Skip an empty vault; avoid a full lint on an unchanged wiki.

Select the calling workflow before mutations; CLI syntax alone does not authorize writes.

# Driving the Obsidian CLI

The vault is targeted by name: `obsidian vault=<name> <command> ...`. wiki-master
resolves `<name>` from `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT_NAME` or the vault folder's basename, and
its **filesystem path** from `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT`, defaulting to `~/.wiki-master-vault`
(this convention lives in `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` — the bundled scripts use it, so
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` and friends need no path argument). Start there rather than
searching the disk for the vault.
`file=` resolves by name (like wikilinks); `path=` is an exact vault-relative path.
Invoke commands through `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. Never bypass it with native CLI calls or run
parallel native commands. The shared lock has a bounded wait; busy means not sent.
Oversized or physically multiline requests are rejected before launch. Ordinary
Markdown bodies go through filesystem editing, even when the CLI works. Do not
chunk a rejected note into repeated CLI writes. Inspect the exact target first if
an earlier write's outcome is uncertain. See the directly linked access contract.
The guarded `vault info=path` command can confirm the root
when the app responds; the known configured/default root supports filesystem access
without that probe.

## Windows invocation — REQUIRED
**Never run `obsidian` from the Bash tool.** The two binaries are Obsidian's own
design, and the official docs explain why: "Windows uses a terminal redirector
that connects Obsidian to stdin/stdout properly. This is necessary because
Obsidian normally runs as a GUI app which is incompatible with terminal outputs
on Windows. When you install Obsidian 1.12.7+ the `Obsidian.com` terminal
redirector will be added in the folder where you installed the `Obsidian.exe`
file."

Windows `PATHEXT` orders `.com` before `.exe`, so PowerShell and Node's
`execFileSync` select the redirector. **Git Bash does not apply `PATHEXT`**, so a
bare `obsidian` there finds the GUI binary, which prints nothing and exits 0 —
which can produce misleading empty output. Use the
**PowerShell tool** or `vault.mjs`. The bundled guard enforces supported invocation.

## Empty is not an answer
Obsidian publishes no exit-code contract and does not document how a command
signals "no results" — neither the official reference nor kepano's first-party
skill says. That gap, not tool unreliability, is why an *empty* result needs one
cheap check before anything is decided on the strength of it.

Probe lazily, never upfront. Run nothing in advance: any command that returns
results has already proven the backend alive — from then on, trust empties too.
Only when a command returns empty **and** that emptiness is about to drive a
decision (report "not ingested", declare no backlinks, skip a page) run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" search query="the" total` — a live backend prints a number, which
means the empty was real; trust it and every later empty without re-probing.
An empty canary means the backend is dead. A session whose commands all return
hits never probes at all.

Two failure modes people assume and neither holds: **the app not running cannot
produce a silent empty** — measured on Windows, a dead app exits 1 with "The CLI
is unable to find Obsidian. Please make sure Obsidian is running and try again."
(the docs claim the first command launches Obsidian; it does not — start it
yourself) — and index-rebuild has never been observed to. Do not cite either as
a reason to distrust a result.

## Syntax and the live contract
- **Parameters take `=`; flags are bare.** `create name="My Note" content="Hello"`
  vs `create name=Note open overwrite`. `\n` / `\t` for multiline content.
- **`vault=<name>` must be the first parameter**, before the command.
- **`format=` is a parameter, not a flag**, and its default varies per command —
  `search` defaults to `text`, `backlinks`/`tags`/`properties` to `tsv`,
  `base:query` to `json`. Never assume JSON; ask for it.
- **`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" help` outranks the docs.** Obsidian's own skill says it "is always
  up to date" — so when the published reference and the binary disagree, the
  binary wins. Check `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" help <command>` before concluding a flag is gone.
- Prior art worth comparing against: kepano (Obsidian's CEO) publishes a
  first-party `obsidian-cli` Agent Skill. Where it and this skill agree — `total`
  for counts, `file=` vs `path=`, vault-first ordering — the agreement is
  independent corroboration, not inheritance.

## Read / search
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" read path=wiki/concepts/alpha.md`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" search query="tag:clippings neural" path=wiki limit=10 format=json`
- Scope to `path=wiki` by default — `raw/` holds immutable source dumps (one
  clipping can contain a long document) and belongs in results only when asked.
- Probe cost before fetching: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" search query="..." total` (a count only).
- **Never default to `search:context`** — it returns every matching line from
  every file, and
  `limit=` bounds files, not lines, so it cannot save you. Escalate to
  `search:context` only with both `path=` and a narrow query.

## Links & graph
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" backlinks file=alpha counts` — who links here
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" links file=alpha` — outgoing links
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" unresolved verbose format=json` — broken links WITH source files.
  The bare form returns targets only; `verbose` is the difference between a
  defect you can act on and a string you can't attribute. Several subcommands
  have lossy defaults with a `verbose` escape — prefer `format=json verbose`.
- **Health metrics come from `scripts/health.mjs`, not from `orphans` /
  `deadends`.** The CLI computes those verdicts with structural files' links
  (index.md links everything, so nothing ever looks orphaned) and offers no
  source-side exclusion. health.mjs builds the graph from the filesystem.

## Typed properties (frontmatter)
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" property:set name=reviewed value=2026-07-15 type=date path=wiki/concepts/alpha.md`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" property:read name=reviewed path=...`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" properties path=...` — list a note's properties

## Create / edit / move
- Create, replace or append ordinary Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits
  under the known root, using the shared operation lifecycle. Preserve current
  content and raw evidence. Do not send substantial text through the CLI.
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" move file=foo to=wiki/entities`

## Tags, tasks, templates, bases
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" tags counts` · `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" tag name=neural verbose`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" base:query file=stale.base view=all format=json`
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" template:insert name=source-note`

## Escape hatches
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" command id=<id>` — run any Obsidian command (`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" commands` to list)
- `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" eval code="<js>"` — arbitrary JS in app context (last resort).
  **This is remote code execution against the vault**, and it sits in the same
  namespace as the read-only subcommands: a blanket `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" *` permission grant
  covers it. It belongs in its own permission decision, not folded in with
  `search` and `read`. The same applies to `dev:cdp` and `dev:debug`.

If a command fails, report its diagnostic and follow the directly linked access
policy. The wrapper defaults to a 10-second timeout and never retries. After a
timed-out mutation, inspect the exact target: the write may have run even though
the response was lost. `assertRunning` is for app-only actions, not a gate on
supported filesystem reads, reports or ordinary Markdown edits.

# Completion for vault mutations

Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.

`index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate it with `index-gen.mjs`,
never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
the fence is preserved. A catalog already dirty from another writer remains
theirs: refresh safe project catalogs separately and report a deferred global
refresh rather than adopt foreign edits merely to close this operation.

**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.

1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>
   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a
   name lost that way is lost without an error.
   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;
   keep the manifest under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. This narrows the
   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
   same file.
   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file
   <ledger>`. There is no override flag. A close with `--paths-file` is unchanged, and
   with no other token open an unscoped close behaves as before. Every refused close
   (this one, a pre-dirty ledger path, an evidence mismatch) appends a counts-only
   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.
   When the ledger carries a receipt that records its own byte length and SHA-256
   (captured JSON or log evidence), also pass `--evidence-map <file>`: a JSON object
   of ledger path to `{ "bytes": N, "sha256": "<64 lower-case hex>" }`, kept beside
   the ledger. After staging and before committing, `op-commit` compares each staged
   blob with its declaration. On a mismatch it commits nothing, unstages, keeps the
   token, and names the file, the declared and stored size and hash, and the exact
   `.gitattributes` line (`<path> -text`) that keeps the bytes. Add that one line,
   list `.gitattributes` in the ledger and rerun. It never edits an attribute itself,
   and ordinary Markdown keeps the vault's text policy. A pass is reported as its own
   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.
   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,
   canonical placement and exact citation/link targets. Preserve raw bodies and
   unrelated changes. `reviewed` advances only for factual verification. On uncertain
   write timeouts inspect the target before retrying; do not make a duplicate page.
4. **Refresh affected catalogs once.** For project authoring run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-catalogs.mjs" --project <slug> --apply` instead of three separate generators. It builds one vault graph, updates only that project's backlog and MOC, then the global index; unchanged files are not rewritten. Leave out `--apply` for a dry run: it writes nothing and its `changed` list is the list an apply would change, and `--diff` prints each changed file's removed and added lines to stderr. With concurrent writers, pass `--paths-file <JSON ownership ledger>` so another writer's uncommitted pages stay out: a page is listed when it is in the last commit or the ledger names it, and a page another writer has only staged is not. A line the catalog already has for such a page, put there by that writer's own run, is kept. Inspect the returned `changed` paths; with `--since <token>`, an `--apply` records them in the operation's ledger (a dry run records nothing). Without a project selector it refreshes all projects. Standalone generators remain available and the project generators accept `--project`. A global scan is still needed for cross-project ambiguous names.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative into `log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title
   "<title>"`. It writes one uniquely named `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md`,
   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
   ledger is how it reaches the close.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,
   read what it lists as unclaimed, then `op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>"
   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.
   The helper attempts a semantic index refresh after committing; inspect notices
   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,
   not a bare `git push`: it fetches, rebases onto the upstream (never a merge commit),
   pushes, retries once when another machine pushed first, and verifies against a fresh
   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.
   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log
   path and verify its actual changed paths rather than assuming its old SHA.
   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the
   user to push work you are responsible for. Inspect outgoing commits first;
   coordinate rather than publish unrelated or explicitly held local commits.
   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.

   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.

   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.

## Recovery and token ownership

- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.

**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.

**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.

**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.

**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`
always carries `opRefusals` as `{ total, preDirty, evidence, unscoped, syncOverlap }`. The
line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.

**Git ownership.** The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.

**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

```sh
(
  export WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault'
  wiki_op_token=$(node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink) || exit
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since "$wiki_op_token" <path>...
  printf '%s\n' 'Validated task narrative' | node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" || exit
  wiki_ledger="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wiki-ledger-$wiki_op_token.json"
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since "$wiki_op_token" --out "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" --paths-file "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs' || exit
)
```
