## Preserving figures (`--figures`)

Text extraction loses every figure, and in a PDF a graph is usually **vector
drawing**, not an embedded image, so `pdfimages` alone misses it. `--figures`
therefore renders **whole pages** with `pdftoppm -r 200 -png` and stores them in the
vault's figure convention.

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --source="<url>" --figures            # auto
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --figures=all | --figures=3,5-7 --figures-max=60
# figures for a clipping that already exists, from a PDF you supply:
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --figures-only --clipping raw/clippings/<name>.md
```

- **Pages chosen.** `auto` (the bare-flag default) selects a page when either holds:
  1. **Raster:** `pdfimages -list` shows an `image` row (not `smask`/`mask`) at least
     100x100 px and 0.75 in on the page, not a logo object repeated on half the pages.
  2. **Vector:** `pdftocairo -svg` shows at least 30 drawing elements outside glyph
     definitions AND the page is text-light (no text layer, or under 80 % of the
     document's median non-space characters per page), or at least 600 drawing
     elements regardless of text. A document whose text is outlined (no text layer
     at all) selects every drawn page. Raster pages skip the slower SVG probe.

  It is deterministic and approximate: box-and-arrow diagrams on text pages are
  caught by the 30-element floor, but a ruled table can be a false positive and a
  figure drawn with very few strokes can be missed. Use `--figures=all` or a page
  list when the choice matters. `all` renders every page; a list renders exactly those.
- **Cap.** At most 40 pages per run (`--figures-max=N` to raise); a truncation is
  reported. Pages are not cropped: sidecars say `crop: full`.
- **Output.** `raw/figures/<clipping-slug>-p<N>.png` plus `<same>.md` with frontmatter
  `source`, `page`, `crop: full`, `dpi: 200`, `sha256`, `captured`,
  `clipping: "[[raw/clippings/<file>.md]]"`, `ai-generated: false`, then `# Title, page N`
  and a one-line machine description naming the candidates detected (`raster`,
  `vector`, or "none detected" for a page chosen by request).
- **Clipping frontmatter.** `figures: ["raw/figures/<slug>-p3.md", ...]` is added to the
  clipping's FRONTMATTER, after `source-hash`. The body is never edited. Only this tool
  writes it; it is pipeline state like `fidelity`.
- **Idempotent.** A page whose PNG hash already matches is left alone; a PNG identical
  to any existing figure is skipped as a duplicate; a sidecar with `crop` other than
  `full` (a hand-cropped figure) is never overwritten.
- **`--figures-only`** needs `--clipping <path>` (vault-relative, absolute or relative).
  It checks the PDF first: `source-hash` hashes the clipping's extracted text, so the
  PDF is re-extracted the way the clipping was and the hashes compared. A mismatch is
  refused (`--allow-pdf-mismatch` overrides); a clipping with no `source-hash` or one
  made by OCR cannot be checked and only warns.
- **Tools.** poppler `pdftoppm` (required), `pdfimages`, `pdftocairo`, `pdfinfo`; found
  on PATH or in the winget poppler folder. Missing tools never fail the clip: the run
  prints what is missing and how to install it (`--doctor` lists it), and `auto`
  degrades to whichever probe is available.
- **Operation bracket.** Figure PNG/sidecars and the clipping's frontmatter edit are
  ordinary vault writes inside the same `op-begin`/`op-commit` as the clip; op-commit
  commits whatever became dirty, so nothing extra is needed. `health.mjs` treats
  `raw/figures/` as assets, not clippings, so they never count toward the ingest backlog
  or as missing a `source-hash`.
- A render is a faithful page, not an interpretation. Describe what a figure shows only
  from looking at it (see [ingestion](ingest.md)).

## Overriding the reading mode

The detector is a heuristic and can misclassify **margin annotations beside a
body column** as a table. Aligned mode can splice a margin note into the adjacent
body line and leave hyphenated breaks unjoined. The result may read as ordinary
prose with only a `fidelity: tabular` caveat while no longer being quotable. **Assume neither mode is
right until you have looked at the output.**

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs" "<file.pdf>" --mode=reading-order --source="<url>"
```

- `auto` (default) — the detector chooses.
- `reading-order` — force reading-order. Correct for prose, two-column papers, and
  body+margin layouts. Joins hyphenated line breaks; reads each column whole.
- `table` — force aligned reading. Correct for a real table. Always floors fidelity
  at `tabular`, because aligned output is reconstructed from horizontal position
  however you arrived at it.

An override that **diverges** from the detector is recorded, not silent: the
clipping is stamped `extraction: reading-order-forced` and the run warns on stderr.
An override that agrees with the detector is a no-op and is not annotated. An
unknown `--mode=` value is an error, and `--mode=table` on a pdftotext without
`-table` is refused rather than quietly downgraded — believing you forced a mode
that was not applied is the failure this whole module exists to prevent.

**How to tell which mode a document wants** — extract two pages both ways and look:

```bash
pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -f 40 -l 41 "<file.pdf>" -            # reading-order
pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -f 40 -l 41 -table "<file.pdf>" -     # aligned
```

If aligned mode puts *unrelated* text on the same line, it is a two-column or
margin layout — use `reading-order`. If reading-order emits a whole key column
followed by a whole value column, it is a table — use `table`.

# Clipping a PowerPoint deck into the wiki

The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only,
`clip-pdf` handles **PDFs**, and `clip-docx`/`clip-xlsx` handle Word documents and
spreadsheets. A `.pptx` slide deck — bullets and tables per slide, plus speaker
notes, not flowing paragraphs — falls to none of those. This reference covers the
PowerPoint path. **The canonical stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never
the binary deck** — that keeps the vault greppable, diffable, and answerable, and
makes `[[note]]` provenance resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an
opaque attachment.

## How it works

`clip-pptx.mjs` extracts each slide's text, tables, and speaker notes with a
bundled Python helper (`scripts/lib/pptx-extract.py`) built on **python-pptx** —
**not** pandoc (pandoc has no `.pptx` input format at all) and **not**
LibreOffice (avoids a heavyweight dependency for this one format). The helper is
invoked via Node's `execFileSync` against the first working interpreter among
`python3`, `python`, `py` (Windows never installs a `python3.exe`, and its
always-on-PATH WindowsApps `python3` alias fails outright). This is a brand-new,
self-contained implementation shipped inside wiki-master — it does **not** shell
out to, or otherwise depend on, any other installed Copilot plugin's copy of
python-pptx glue, so wiki-master stays portable across machines regardless of
what else is installed.

Output is one `## Slide N` heading per slide (emitted even for a slide with no
extractable text, so slide numbering matches the real deck — useful for citing
"slide 7 says X"), followed by bullet/paragraph text, any table rendered as a
markdown table, and a `**Speaker notes:**` line when present. Then
`clip-pptx.mjs` writes `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with the standard clipping
frontmatter (`source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`, `source-hash`).
It skips duplicates and prior declines, and records a decline for a **thin**
extraction (empty or near-empty deck) so it is not retried blindly.

**Legacy `.ppt` (binary PowerPoint 97-2003) is explicitly unsupported** —
python-pptx cannot read that format at all. `clip-pptx.mjs` detects the `.ppt`
extension and fails clearly, telling you to convert to `.pptx` first, rather than
attempting extraction and reporting a confusing downstream error.

## Steps

1. **Preflight** (once): confirm python-pptx is installed. Probe the same
   candidates the clipper does, in order, and use the FIRST that succeeds:
   `python3 -c "import pptx"`, then `python -c "import pptx"`, then
   `py -c "import pptx"`. On Windows a bare `python3` may be the WindowsApps
   alias stub, which fails even when Python and python-pptx are correctly
   installed — so a `python3` failure alone does NOT mean the library is missing.
   If every candidate fails, tell the user to run `<interpreter> -m pip install
   python-pptx` (naming the interpreter that will run the helper — installing into
   a different one is the classic silent failure) and stop; do not fabricate content.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for PowerPoint decks):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pptx.mjs" "<path/to/file.pptx>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - `--source` is the citable origin. Omit for a purely local file and the file
     path is recorded as the source.
   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run,
     so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is recorded
     going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so a clip made without it
     is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it only when there is no
     research run behind the clip; never invent one.
   - A `thin` or `failed` result means the deck is empty/corrupt/protected, or is
     a legacy `.ppt` — report it for manual handling; do not invent the text.
3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and sanity-check
   the slide text and any tables against the deck. Extraction drops slide design,
   layout, images, and chart *rendering* — table cell text is preserved, but a
   chart's visual is not.
4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization.

## Guardrails

- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only.
- `clip-pptx.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for PowerPoint decks — the
  model never writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and
  hashing).
- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of the wrong deck is still
  wrong; extraction also drops slide design/layout/images and chart rendering —
  verify quotes against the deck before they land on a wiki page (guardrail #5).
- Legacy `.ppt` is unsupported — convert to `.pptx` first; do not attempt a
  workaround extraction.

# Clipping a spreadsheet into the wiki

The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only,
`clip-pdf` handles **PDFs**, and `clip-docx` handles **Word** documents. A
workbook — sheets of cells, where meaning lives in which value sits against
which label — falls to none of those. This reference covers the spreadsheet path.
**The canonical stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never the binary
workbook** — that keeps the vault greppable, diffable and answerable, and makes
`[[note]]` provenance resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an
opaque attachment.

**Never reach a workbook by converting it to PDF and running `clip-pdf`.** That
is the exact case `clip-pdf` warns about: row/label pairings get rebuilt from
horizontal position, and a flattened table reads clean while pairing the wrong
number with the wrong label. A spreadsheet is the worst document to put through
it, because the pairing *is* the content.

## How it works

`clip-xlsx.mjs` converts with **LibreOffice** (`soffice --headless --convert-to
html`, which renders every sheet as a table), then pipes that HTML through
**pandoc** to Markdown with `--wrap=none`, and writes `raw/clippings/<slug>.md`
with the standard clipping frontmatter (`source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`,
`quality`, `source-hash`). The title is derived from the filename — a workbook
carries no title worth trusting.

- **`soffice` is invoked by bare name on purpose**, so PATHEXT selects the
  console shim (`soffice.com`); `soffice.exe` is the GUI build and writes nothing
  to stdout. Both converters run through Node's `execFileSync` — do **not** shell
  out to them from a Bash tool.
- **Two failures that look alike are handled differently.** A missing LibreOffice
  is fatal and stops the run with an install pointer: fix the install. A workbook
  that *itself* fails to convert (corrupt or password-protected) returns `failed`
  so a batch run continues. Report it for manual handling; never invent the cells.
- **Duplicates are caught by content hash**, not just by path, so a renamed or
  moved workbook whose contents the vault already holds is recognized rather than
  clipped twice under a second slug.

## Steps

1. **Preflight** (once): confirm both converters are installed — `soffice
   --version` and `pandoc -v`. If LibreOffice is missing, tell the user to
   install it (https://www.libreoffice.org/download/) and stop; do not fabricate
   cell values or retype the workbook by hand.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for workbooks):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<path/to/file.xlsx>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - `--source` is the citable origin. Omit it for a purely local file and the
     file path is recorded as the source; never invent a URL to fill the field.
   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run,
     so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is recorded
     going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so a clip made without it
     is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it only when there is no
     research run behind the clip; never invent one.
   - `--quality` is your credibility judgment of the workbook as a source, which
     is separate from how cleanly it extracted.
3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and confirm the
   sheets came through as real tables with their labels still attached to their
   values. Conversion is lossy on formulas, merged cells, charts and multi-row
   headers — it captures rendered values, not the model behind them.
   - A `thin` result (under 100 words) records a decline so it is not retried
     blindly. **Unlike `clip-docx`, this clipper has no `--allow-short`
     override** — a genuinely tiny but complete workbook needs the decline
     cleared or the content captured another way. Say so rather than pretending
     the clip succeeded.
4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires
   authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization.

## Guardrails

- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only.
- `clip-xlsx.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for workbooks — the model never
  writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline and hashing, and
  the ingest backlog joins on exactly that hash).
- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of the wrong workbook is still
  wrong, and a converted sheet can silently lose the structure that gave a number
  its meaning — verify any figure against the workbook before it lands on a wiki
  page (guardrail #5).

# Discover sources on a topic

Given a topic, find and independently assess sources that fill an evidence gap.
Perspective passes return candidates and never write the vault. A candidates-only
request stays read-only: report the selection without declines or captures. When
capture is within scope, use [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources).
Ingestion is a separate authorized mode.

## Independence checkpoint before capture

Topic discovery requires the five perspective passes below and independent
selection. When the host provides delegation, actually dispatch read-only
finders; do not replace their execution with a list you found and scored yourself.
The orchestrator may select their returned candidates, or a separate reviewer
may select them. A finder must not grade its own finds. A small or controlled
source corpus does not remove this separation.

Before opening an operation or calling a clipper, retain the returned candidate
lists and the independent selection with its credibility reasons. If delegation
is unavailable, use the documented sequential lenses and disclose that limit;
do not claim an independent pass that did not run. Named-source capture skips
topic discovery and uses [capture](capture.md) directly.

## Phase 0 — dedup before searching
Gather what the wiki already has so the search hunts for *gaps*, not dupes:
- Known source URLs: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs"` prints
  them, one per line, normalized as the clipper normalizes them (`--count` prints
  the number). It reads the clippings themselves (the first `source:` line of each
  file directly under `raw/clippings`), rather than querying an index built from
  them — the shortest path to the fact, and it stays correct while the index is
  stale. To ask about particular candidates, use
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`: one line
  per URL, in the order given, `new`, `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md` (with
  ` (+N recapture)` when later captures of the page exist) or `declined: <reason>`.
  `--summary --topic "<topic>"` prints what a topic already holds. All three only read.
- Coverage summary: name the unanswered question, run bounded wiki searches, and
  read the relevant task MOC and leading concept/synthesis pages. Read only the
  manual Start here section of `index.md` if orientation is needed; do not load
  the generated catalog. List the known coverage and the specific evidence gap.
- Sanity-check the set: if the vault has clippings on disk but the known-URL
  set is empty, STOP — the collection step failed; do not proceed to search.
Pass the known-URL set + a one-line "already covered" summary to every perspective.

## Phase 1 — five perspective researchers (parallel if supported, else sequential)
Each perspective gets: the topic, the known-URL set, the coverage summary, and its
lens. Run them **in parallel if your host supports agent fan-out** — Claude Code:
dispatch five read-only agents in one message via the Agent tool; Copilot CLI: use
custom agents — **otherwise run the five lenses sequentially yourself.** Each runs
2–3 *varied* web searches, pre-skips any result whose domain is on the blocklist,
fetches the promising hits, and **returns a ranked candidate list** — it writes
nothing. Lenses:
- **Academic** — papers, textbooks, primary research, .edu.
- **Technical** — official docs, specs, standards, source repos.
- **Applied** — case studies, real-world usage, tutorials from practitioners.
- **News/Trends** — recent developments, reputable reporting (last ~2 years).
- **Contrarian** — critiques, failure modes, dissenting analysis.

Each candidate: `{ title, url, quality_guess: high|medium|low, key_findings,
why_ingest, adds_evidence, changes_page }`. `adds_evidence` names the unanswered
question it helps settle; `changes_page` names an existing or proposed concept
or synthesis. More material on an already answered question is not automatically
an improvement. Inspect existing high-use stubs and missing bridges before
requesting another broad collection run.

## Phase 2 — independent select + credibility (do NOT let a finder grade itself)
As the orchestrator (or a separate reviewer), over the pooled candidates:
1. Dedup by URL (normalize: drop `#fragment`, trailing `/`); drop any already in the
   known-URL set; drop blocked domains; drop any in the decline log
   (`.wiki-master/declined.json` — clip.mjs enforces this too, but skipping here
   saves re-arguing settled candidates).
2. Score each survivor with the rubric → `high | medium | low`:
   - +2 peer-reviewed / primary / official
   - +1 recent (≤3 yr) where recency matters
   - +1 known/credentialed author or authoritative org
   - +1 corroborated by another perspective's find (max +1)
   - −1 vendor-primary / promotional / single-blogger opinion
   Tiers: **high** ≥4, **medium** 2–3, **low** 0–1, **reject** <0 (don't clip).
3. Keep the top sources (favor `high`/`medium`; a few `low` are fine if on-topic).
   Reddit posts/comments and Medium articles are eligible; assess each source
   using the rubric, without treating votes as credibility. In the ranked report,
   group them under `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and `## Medium articles`
   respectively, and carry those sections into ingestion per the
   [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium).
4. **Only when capture is authorized, before the first decline or clip write**, open a discover operation with
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` and retain its
   token using the host-specific completion example. Reuse that operation below, and
   pass its token as `--since <token>` on every clip: each clipper then records the exact
   path of every file it writes in the operation's ledger.
   **Record every reject** so it is never re-litigated:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<one-line reason>"`.
   "Seen, considered, declined" must have a representation — an unrecorded reject
   is indistinguishable from "never seen" and comes back every run. Declines
   expire after 180 days (TTL), so a changed world gets one re-evaluation.
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/decline.mjs" list` (`--json` for a machine reading)
   and `show "<url>"` read the log without changing it. `supersede "<url>" --reason "<why>"`
   ends an active decline without clipping anything; it is the only way to do so for a URL
   already in the vault, because `--supersede-decline` on a clip takes effect only when a
   clipping is written.


Continue with [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources)
for approved-scope survivors, or return the candidate report for a research-only
request. Named URLs and saved files use [named capture](capture.md) directly.

# Ingest captured evidence

For a requested research → ingest → search-and-answer flow, complete ingestion
below and then follow [wiki-user](../../wiki-user/SKILL.md),
[search](../../wiki-user/references/search.md), and
[query](../../wiki-user/references/query.md). Run the search helper against the
updated vault before answering and inspect returned passages and exact evidence.
Lexical search works without a semantic index. Report unavailable channels;
reading the pages you just wrote does not replace the requested retrieval step.
Ordinary ingestion alone does not require this additional answer workflow.

Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) before creating or merging a concept, alias or relationship; [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) when you compute the backlog with the content-hash join, or hit a structural repair.
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

## Select eligible work before opening an operation

For an explicit request to process new/un-ingested clippings without a filename,
run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`. The **not ingested
(no summary records their hash)** list is the starting set. This source-hash join,
including its documented legacy fallback, is authoritative for membership; do
not infer backlog from filenames, navigation citations or a successful exit.
An unspecified request to use the researcher role is not a request to ingest all.

For named clippings, resolve and read those exact paths only. Check the same
hash-join report and the existing source summaries before doing work: if a source
page already records that clipping's `source-hash`, preserve it and report already
ingested. A rerun creates no duplicate summary or unearned second ingestion.
An explicit request to revise an existing summary can update that canonical page;
do not expand named ingestion to unrelated backlog or broad discovery.

Inspect each selected clipping's metadata before treating it as support. Exclude
`citation-status: quarantined`, `restricted` or `retired` evidence, preserving its
raw bytes and restriction; report it separately rather than summarizing it as
accepted support. A missing source hash is a repair issue, not permission to
invent one. Binary originals and figure sidecars are not summary targets. The
helper's backlog can include restricted or defective captures, so its count is
not automatically the count of eligible work.

If the backlog is zero, every named source is already summarized, or no eligible
source remains, stop and report the actual result and any exclusions. Do not
create pages, open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes. For work that
remains, retain the exact eligible set and initial hash-join membership. See
[backlog semantics](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) for migration
and repair cases; structural repair still needs its own authorized scope.

## Ingest and complete the selected set

Read [operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
before the first authorized write.

**Open the operation first:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op ingest`
This records what was already uncommitted, so the commit at the end contains your
work and not the user's in-progress writing. Close it in step 6.

**Keep the ledger as you go.** Record each page you write (`wiki/sources/...`, a concept
or synthesis you create or change) with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <path>...`, and give
`--since <token>` to `index-gen.mjs` and `log-entry.mjs`. When this ingest follows a discover
run, take the clipping set from that run's ledger file (its `raw/clippings/...` entries), not
from `git show`. Delegated writers get the parent token in their brief and run the same `add`
for the pages they write; they never close the operation (see the operations reference).

Prefer a named clipping set; two concurrent ingests can overwrite shared concept
pages, so coordinate overlapping targets rather than processing the global backlog
in parallel. Update only pages substantively changed by the evidence.

Apply the [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium)
to every page you write: Reddit-derived content belongs under
`## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and Medium-derived content under
`## Medium articles`, including when updating a mixed-source page.

For each eligible source, perform steps 1–3 and preserve raw body bytes. After
the selected batch, perform steps 4–6 once so the operation has one log and commit:
1. Read the exact clipping through the guarded CLI or filesystem. Write derived
   Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits, never a whole CLI `content=` payload. Discuss
   the key takeaways with the user.
2. Write/update `wiki/sources/<slug>.md`: a summary with `sources: ["[[<raw link>]]"]`,
   `type: source`, `ai-generated: true`, and typed `created`/`updated`/`reviewed`.
   **Always quote each wikilink inside the list — `sources: ["[[A]]", "[[B]]"]`,
   never a bare `sources: [[A]]` or an unquoted block list (`- [[A]]`).** Both
   unquoted shapes look correct and Obsidian still renders the links, but neither
   is valid YAML: `[[A]]` is flow-sequence syntax one level too many and silently
   parses into a nested list instead of a string, which is exactly the "type
   mismatch, expected list" defect `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-inline-sources.mjs"`
   exists to repair in bulk. Quoting is what makes it an unambiguous string.
   **Cite the clipping by its actual filesystem path — `sources: ["[[raw/clippings/<exact filename>.md]]"]` — copied from the path you just read, never retyped from
   the source's title.** The clipper slugifies a title into a filename (`/`, `:`,
   `#`, `*`, `?`, quotes and brackets all become `-`, then a 120-char cap), so any
   title carrying one of those characters or running long does NOT name its own
   file. Citing the remembered title produces a link to a file that does not exist:
   the page becomes a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, even
   though the ingest itself was correct. List the resolved vault's exact `raw/clippings/` directory or reuse the path
   from step 1 rather than reconstructing it.
   Also record `source-hashes: [<sha256>, …]` — the `source-hash` frontmatter value
   of each clipping you summarized (read it from the clipping's frontmatter). This
   is the machine key the ingest-backlog metric joins on — immune to filename and
   citation drift; the `sources: ["[[…]]"]` wikilink stays for navigation.
   To repair vaults that already drifted this way:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"` (dry run) then `--apply`.
   **Figures.** If the clipping's frontmatter lists `figures:`, open each sidecar
   (`raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.md`) and **look at the PNG with the Read tool** before
   writing. Embed the ones that carry evidence on the source page as
   `![[raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.png]]` next to the claim they support, with a sentence
   saying what the figure shows (axes, series, trend) taken from what you see, not from
   the machine description. A page render is a whole page: say which part matters.
   Quote numbers read off a chart as approximate and attribute them. If the PDF has
   figures but no `figures:`, tell the user `clip-pdf.mjs --figures-only` can add them.
   Never edit or add to `raw/figures/`.
3. Before creating a concept, search the proposed title, equivalent wording and
   nearby passages. Extend the canonical page, add a genuinely equivalent alias,
   or explain the new concept's distinct scope. Use `_templates/concept-note.md`;
   follow the directly linked efficacy reference for aliases and relationships.
   Create a stub (`status: stub`) only for an identified gap. Explain each useful
   connection under `## Relationships`; keep supporting citations in `sources:`
   and the relevant prose. Relatedness does not establish support. Update the
   task map the new knowledge helps answer. Preserve `reviewed` on pages that
   received only metadata/link edits; stamp it only after factual verification.
4. Regenerate the catalog: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-gen.mjs"`
   (never hand-edit index.md's generated fence). With another writer in the vault,
   add `--paths-file <ledger>` (the JSON array of pages this ingest wrote, from
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`) so their
   uncommitted pages stay out of the catalog and their lines already in it stay in. Write the log entry by piping the
   narrative to `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op ingest --title "<title>" --since <token>`
   (creates `log/<timestamp>-ingest-<slug>.md` in the resolved vault).
5. Never edit anything under `raw/`. Validate the derived pages' exact citation
   targets, source hashes, frontmatter and supported claims. Rerun
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog` and compare the actual
   hash-join membership with the initial set. Eligible sources just summarized
   should leave that set; restricted captures do not become ingested by exclusion.
   Confirm already summarized sources and raw bodies remain unchanged.
6. **Close the operation:**
   Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>` and read what it lists as
   unclaimed (another writer's pages, or one of yours you did not record), then
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op ingest --title "<what you ingested>" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`
   Commits exactly the pages this ingest touched, as one revertable unit, and
   reports anything it deliberately left alone. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Then follow the shared completion contract to push your updates (`wiki-sync.mjs`, or `wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<what you ingested>"` to close and push in one command) and verify remote publication. If the sync is refused because uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (exit 3), read "Refused sync" in the [operations reference](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md): never reset, check out, stash or delete a file you did not write.

---
name: wiki-researcher
description: Use when asked to discover external sources for the wiki, capture a named URL or file as evidence, clip PDF, Word, PowerPoint, spreadsheet, GitHub repository or authenticated Confluence sources, ingest named existing clippings, or process new/un-ingested clippings. A backlog count is maintainer reporting; ordinary web or application work is not a wiki research request.
---

# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `$ARGUMENTS` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. When delegation is available, use separate
  read-only finders and keep the selector independent of the sources it found.
  Complete that selection before opening a capture operation; a self-selected
  list does not fulfill independent research. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

If the requested flow continues with search or an answer after ingestion, hand
off to [wiki-user](../wiki-user/SKILL.md): load its
[search](../wiki-user/references/search.md) and, for a cited answer,
[query](../wiki-user/references/query.md) procedures. Actually run retrieval
against the updated vault and open the returned passages; do not substitute
memory of the pages just written. A missing semantic index still permits lexical
search and must be reported, not used as a reason to skip retrieval. This final
answer remains read-only unless filing it was separately authorized.

# Author original wiki documentation

Read directly for this operation: [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), [operations](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md).
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

For: $ARGUMENTS

Steps:
1. Identify the project and document kind using the canonical placement table below. Locate the existing page first; preserve its established filename.
   For a new project, create its `overview.md` before its other documents.
2. Read the existing page and relevant project behavior. Before writing that the
   vault holds no source or page on a topic, run two bounded `search.mjs` queries
   (the topic, and the key terms of the claim) and report "not found by these queries",
   naming them; when a query returns a source page, cite it. Open before writing:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op relink`.
   Save the token using the PowerShell or POSIX example in the operations reference. Create new files only after opening, never before: a page written first counts as already dirty, and `op-commit` refuses it until you pass `--include`.
3. Use `_templates/authored-note.md`, `_templates/authored-decision.md`, or
   `_templates/authored-backlog-item.md` as appropriate. Set `type: authored`,
   `sources: []`, honest `ai-generated`, and matching `project:`/`kind:` metadata.
   Write ordinary Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits, even when the
   Obsidian app is healthy; never send a whole note body through CLI `content=`.
   A stopped app does not prevent authoring. After an uncertain
   CLI write, inspect the target before retrying.
4. Revise living content in place; never stack dated update paragraphs. Keep
   architecture as-built, roadmaps current, ADR consequences balanced and
   reconstructed decisions labeled. Set `updated`; preserve `reviewed` unless
   factual content or project behavior was actually verified.
5. Validate frontmatter, placement and links of exactly the pages this task wrote.
   Use full-path links when crossing project boundaries:
   `[[wiki/authored/<project>/roadmap.md|<project> roadmap]]`. Record each page you
   created or edited with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <saved-token> <path>...`,
   then write the ledger, a JSON array file of those vault-relative paths (kept under
   `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault), with
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>`, and run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`
   with the vault set as in the access reference. Exit 1 means defects: fix, rerun,
   then continue. The ledger format, exit codes, rules and limits are in the
   [authoring reference](#validating-what-a-task-wrote).
6. Refresh affected catalogs with `refresh-catalogs.mjs --project <slug> --apply` (one graph
   scan for the project's backlog, MOC and global index). With concurrent writers pass
   `--paths-file <ledger>` to omit their untracked additions, and `--since <saved-token>`
   so the paths it changes are recorded. Inspect the returned `changed` paths, rewrite the
   ledger with `op-ledger.mjs show`, and when the refresh added paths, rerun step 5's check. If the result lists `staleCatalogs`, other projects' generated
   catalogs now hold a bare link your pages made ambiguous: refresh each named project too.
7. Complete the shared operations contract: one relink log entry (with `--since <saved-token>`),
   then `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>` once more and read what it
   lists as unclaimed, then
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op relink --title "<summary>" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
   A close with no `--paths-file` is refused while another operation is open. Verify the commit and index-refresh notices, push with `wiki-sync.mjs`
   (or close and push in one command with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<summary>"`), and
   verify that the update reached the configured upstream. The authoring request
   includes this completion step unless the user explicitly holds publication;
   do not ask another routine permission question or leave the push to the user.
   If the sync is refused because uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (exit 3), read "Refused sync" in the
   [operations reference](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md): never reset, check out, stash or delete a file you did not write.

**Done only when** the requested documentation and affected catalogs are
validated, its log and operation commit are recorded, and remote publication is
verified. Report explicit holds, local-only results and failed sync precisely;
do not call a local commit published.

## Canonical placement for original project documentation

- **`wiki/authored/`** is where original, primary content lives — advisory
  documentation, policy, house style, or any other work you're writing directly
  into the vault rather than deriving from a captured source. It is not a
  special case of the pipeline: it declares `sources: []` (the vault's existing
  disclosure for "rests on no external artifact," extended here as the default
  for the whole category) and is otherwise a wiki page like any other — living,
  revisable, never needing a `raw/` counterpart.

  **When this page belongs to a multi-doc project**, it lives at
  `wiki/authored/<project>/[<subproject>/]<file>.md` — a real folder, not just a
  frontmatter tag, so related documents stay together. Every doc-kind has one canonical location, so the same request always
  resolves the same way, for every project, without re-deriving convention from
  whatever a prior session happened to name things:

  | You hear | It lives at |
  |---|---|
  | "update the product documentation" / "the overview" | `<project>/overview.md` |
  | "document the architecture" | `<project>/architecture.md` |
  | "add/update the roadmap" | `<project>/roadmap.md` — **mostly generated**, see below |
  | "write a user guide" | `<project>/guides/user.md` |
  | "write a developer guide" | `<project>/guides/developer.md` |
  | "write an administrator guide" | `<project>/guides/administrator.md` |
  | "get me a diagram [for X]" | `<project>/diagrams/<x-slug>.md` |
  | "write up a reference doc on X" | `<project>/reference/<x-slug>.md` |
  | "record a decision about X" (ADR) | `<project>/decisions/<x-slug>-adr.md` |
  | "make a note about X" | `<project>/notes/<x-slug>.md` |
  | "add an item to the backlog" | `<project>/backlog/<item-slug>.md` — see below |

  Set `project:` (a slug, one `/` deep at most for a sub-project, e.g.
  `acme-suite/migrator`) and `kind:` — one of `overview | architecture |
  reference | guide | diagram | decision | roadmap | note | backlog-item` —
  matching the folder you placed it in; both are optional and can be omitted
  for a genuinely standalone, project-less note. Use `_templates/authored-note.md`
  to start a page (`_templates/authored-decision.md` for an ADR,
  `_templates/authored-backlog-item.md` for a backlog item — see below).
  A project's `overview.md` may carry `repo:` (a git remote URL, `owner/name`, or a
  repository folder name; a list is allowed). `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/session-brief.mjs"`, run in
  a repository, uses it to find the project that repository belongs to and print its
  state page; the repository itself needs no change, and holds no project name.
  `kind: decision` additionally carries `decision-status: proposed | accepted |
  superseded | deprecated` (Nygard's ADR vocabulary) — keep it in sync with
  whatever the page's own `## Status` section says in prose. **Existing files
  are not renamed to fit this table** — only new ones follow it going forward;
  a bare canonical leaf name (`overview.md`) repeated across every project would
  be a guaranteed cross-project wikilink collision (see the identity rules below), so existing filenames stay as they are, just moved into
  their project's folder.

  Because `overview.md` / `architecture.md` / `roadmap.md` are deliberately
  reused bare names across projects (each project gets its own), a bare
  `[[roadmap]]` link is ambiguous the moment a **second** project acquires one —
  it resolves to whichever one Obsidian's name index happens to pick, silently,
  with no error. **Any reference to one of these files from *outside* its own
  project must use the piped form naming the full path** —
  `[[wiki/authored/<project>/roadmap.md|<project> roadmap]]` — the same
  convention this vault already uses for other ambiguous bare titles (e.g.
  citing two source pages with the same title). A link from *within* the same
  project's own pages can stay bare.

  Two rules decide a bare name before it counts as ambiguous. A file whose own name equals the link outranks files that only share that name as a `title:` or alias (a site that serves a case's syllabus and opinion under one title gives two clippings one title; the clipping named for the link is the one Obsidian opens). And in navigation a project's generated hub MOC (`moc/<project>.md`) yields to a page of the same name, so a bare `[[<project>]]` reaches the entity page; the MOC is still reached by `[[moc/<project>]]`. Two files with the same name stay ambiguous. After a refresh scoped to one project, the result's `staleCatalogs` names other projects' generated catalogs whose bare link your new pages made ambiguous; refresh each named project.

  **The backlog is a folder of small items, never one growing document.** A
  tracked item is its own file, `<project>/backlog/<item-slug>.md`
  (`kind: backlog-item`, `backlog-status: planned | in-progress | shipped |
  blocked | dropped`). "Add an item" = create exactly one new small file.
  "Update an item" = edit exactly that one file's `backlog-status:` and body —
  **never append a new dated "Update (date): ..." paragraph on top of the old
  ones; edit the item's own text in place.** `git log`/`git blame` is the
  changelog now, not a stack of callouts inside the body. `<project>/roadmap.md`
  itself becomes a thin, mostly-generated index over `backlog/*.md` (run
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-gen.mjs" --apply` after adding/updating an item) —
  the same fenced-region contract `index.md` already uses: hand-written framing
  prose stays outside the fence, the itemized, always-current list lives inside
  it. Revise each item's current state in place so the roadmap stays a useful
  index rather than accumulating dated updates.

  **A backlog item can say what it waits on.** List its prerequisites under `depends-on` as quoted wikilinks to other backlog items of the same project, for example `depends-on: ["[[other-item]]"]` (one scalar or a block sequence also works). A prerequisite is met once its item is shipped or dropped. The relation never changes the item's own status: a `blocked` item you set by hand stays under Blocked. The generated roadmap notes "waiting on" after each open item that has an unmet prerequisite, and lists every planned item whose declared prerequisites are all met under a trailing "Ready to start" section. An item that declares nothing is startable and is not listed there. A prerequisite in another project is rejected; keep the relation inside one project and link across projects in the item's text.

  **List the backlog by lifecycle, not by page status.** Every backlog file has two fields that look alike: the page `status` (`draft` or `maintained`) and the lifecycle `backlog-status`, so a search for `status:` lists no planned items. `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-list.mjs" [--project <name>] [--backlog-status planned,in-progress] [--startable] [--json]` is read-only, does not build the whole-vault graph, and prints one tab-separated line per item: project, lifecycle status, path, title, and `waiting on <items>` when a prerequisite is unmet. `--backlog-status` takes the five words above and `unrecognized` (the items a generated roadmap lists under "Unrecognized status"); `--startable` keeps planned items with no unmet prerequisite, whether or not they declare any. Exit 2 is bad input.

  **A mature project can shorten its generated roadmap.** Two settings in the roadmap's own frontmatter, both off until you add them, so nothing changes by default: `backlog-titles: true` shows each item's first heading as its link text, and `backlog-shipped: collapse` replaces the Shipped list with a count and a link to a generated sibling page, `roadmap-shipped.md` (kind `reference`, created on first use, with its own fenced list). Run `backlog-gen.mjs --apply` or `refresh-catalogs.mjs` after changing a setting. A pipe or bracket in a heading is replaced by a space in the link text. Removing the collapse setting lists Shipped on the roadmap again but leaves `roadmap-shipped.md` for you to delete.

  **A friction item says what produced its observation.** When an item states a behavior as tested or observed, paste the exact call arguments (or the script name) and the exact log or error text beside the claim, and mark a fact whose reading of the source disagrees with the run as unsettled until a run decides. Without them the claim cannot be reconciled with the source later without a rerun.

  When `backlog-gen.mjs` (or `refresh-catalogs.mjs`) creates a roadmap that does not exist, the page starts with `type: authored`, `created`, `updated`, `status: draft`, `sources: []`, `ai-generated: true`, `project` and `kind: roadmap`. `reviewed` is omitted on purpose: nobody has reviewed a page a script just wrote. `created` and `updated` are the UTC day of the run and cannot be set from the command line. A dry run creates no page and no temp file. An existing roadmap is never rewritten outside the generated fence.

  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"`'s `monolith candidates` line (a `wiki/authored/`
  page over ~3,000 words with several stacked dated-update callouts) is a
  secondary safety net for anything that still grows despite the format above —
  report it, don't silently keep appending.

## Keeping project documentation honest

The table above settles *where* a document goes. These settle whether it is still
worth reading a month later — each one is a failure that actually happens, not a
style preference.

- **`architecture.md` is as-built, not as-planned.** The moment it describes
  something that does not exist, a reader cannot tell which half is true. Anything
  intended rather than shipped belongs in `roadmap.md` or a backlog item.
- **`roadmap.md` records state, not history.** It is the page most likely to be
  silently stale, and the failure is specific: it keeps listing as "next" three
  things that shipped a fortnight ago. **Update it in the same operation as the
  work** — a roadmap updated later is a roadmap updated never.
- **An ADR states context, decision, consequences — good AND bad — and status.**
  *A consequences section that lists only benefits is a sales pitch, not a record.*
  The reason to revisit a decision is always in the half that gets left out, so an
  ADR without costs has thrown away the only part that will matter.
- **Label a retrospective ADR as reconstructed.** Most projects start by writing up
  decisions already taken; that is legitimate and lossy. Reasoning recovered from
  code and commit history is not the reasoning that was used, and saying so is the
  difference between a record and a plausible story.
- **Record the failures.** Stalls, refuted hypotheses, and measurements that
  contradicted a confident diagnosis are the highest-value content in a project
  set, because they are precisely what nobody remembers and everybody repeats. If a
  fix was wrong twice before it was right, all three attempts belong on the page.
- **Distinguish "not built" from "built and broken".** From outside they look
  identical and only one of them is a bug. A reader who cannot tell will either
  re-implement something that exists or file a bug against something that does not.
- **The wiki owns intent; the repo owns behaviour.** When they disagree, the code
  wins on what happens and the wiki wins on what was meant — and the disagreement
  itself is worth writing down, because it is usually where the next defect is.

## Validating what a task wrote

Before committing, check exactly the pages the task wrote:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`,
with the vault set as in the access reference.

**The ledger** is the file `op-commit.mjs --paths-file` takes: a non-empty JSON array
of vault-relative paths with `/` separators (no drive prefix, backslash, empty segment,
`.` or `..`), for example `["wiki/authored/demo/guides/user.md","wiki/authored/demo/roadmap.md"]`.
Record each page you wrote with `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <path>...` (the log and
catalog scripts record theirs when given `--since`), then
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <token> --out <ledger>`
writes this file and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong (a path that was already
dirty before `op-begin`, a path that is not dirty now, a changed path nobody recorded). Writing
it by hand with your file tool still works. Keep it under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. A path with no file at that exact spelling is reported as `missing-file`: a page that
does not exist, or one whose letter case or Unicode form differs from the file on disk,
because a case-insensitive disk would otherwise drop that page's link checks without a word.

**The result.** The command writes nothing and reads the whole vault (ambiguity is
vault-wide), but reports only ledger pages; `health.mjs` stays the whole-vault check.
Exit 0 is clean, 1 means defects (fix and rerun), 2 means an unusable ledger, unknown
flag or missing vault. The text report is one `path:line rule message` line per defect,
sorted by path then line, then `validate-authored: N pages checked, M defects`, with
`, K skipped` appended only when K is above zero (checked plus skipped is the number of
distinct ledger paths). `--json` prints
`{"version":1,"checked":N,"skipped":K,"defects":[{"path","line","rule","message"}]}`
instead, which is exactly what `validateAuthored()` in `scripts/validate-authored.mjs` returns. An absent frontmatter key is reported at line 1; a blank key at its own line.

**Public pages.** A page written for a plugin's public repository must not name other projects or machines. `--terms-file <path>` (the owner's private list, kept outside every repository; the file `scripts/scan-private-terms.mjs` reads) adds a `private-term` defect for each ledger page whose text matches a term or a built-in machine pattern (a home-directory path, a GPU model, an invisible character), at its line, naming the rule number and never the text. `--terms-projects a,b` limits the check to pages whose `project:` (first segment) is listed, so a private project's own pages may name themselves. Without `--terms-file` the output is unchanged.

Under `wiki/authored/`:

- `missing-key`: `type`, `created`, `updated`, `status`, `ai-generated` and a
  `sources` line (`[]` is valid) must be present and not blank, so an unfilled
  template fails. A page in a project folder also needs `project` and `kind`, a
  decision `decision-status`, a backlog item `backlog-status`. `reviewed` is optional.
  A page missing one of those two statuses is judged by its declared `kind`, not its folder.
- `bad-value`: `type` is `authored`, `ai-generated` is `true` or `false`, and `kind`
  and the two statuses use the vocabularies above (the message lists them). The page
  `status` is checked for presence only, so `status: wip` passes: check its value
  yourself against `stub`, `draft` and `maintained`.
- `kind-folder-mismatch`, `project-folder-mismatch`: `kind` agrees with the folder
  or file in the table above, `project` with the project folder (case ignored). The
  project is the folder path above the first kind folder (`guides`, `diagrams`,
  `reference`, `decisions`, `notes`, `backlog`) below the top folder, so
  `notes/<topic>/x.md` is a note and `project` must equal that folder path exactly.
  With no kind folder, `project` may be the top folder or the top folder plus one
  sub-project. `overview.md`, `architecture.md` and `roadmap.md` expect their own
  kind when they sit in a project folder. A page directly under `wiki/authored/` has
  no project or kind expectation. A wrong-kind page in `backlog/` gets only
  `kind-folder-mismatch`.

- `dependency-dangling`, `dependency-cross-project`, `dependency-self`, `dependency-cycle`,
  `dependency-malformed`, `dependency-misplaced`: a `depends-on` entry must be a
  wikilink to an existing backlog item of the same project (a note in `backlog/` is
  not an item). The message names the entry; a cycle names the whole loop and is
  reported on each ledger page in it. `dependency-misplaced` is `depends-on` on a page
  that is not a backlog item, where it is ignored. Only the item's own project backlog
  folder is read, so these checks add no second whole-vault scan.

On every wiki content page: `ambiguous-link`, `malformed-link` (a hard-wrapped link
is one), `unresolved-citation`, `malformed-frontmatter` (the page's metadata is not
read because of a stray carriage return or an unclosed fence), `missing-evidence`,
`cites-retired-page` (the cited page is marked `citation-status: retired`, so it is not support)
and `unresolved-link`, which is
stricter than health (it keeps such links as unscored forward links): a task must
not leave a dead link. Code spans and fences are not scanned. An absent file is
`missing-file`; raw, log, template, root catalog, non-Markdown and dot-prefixed paths
are skipped and counted.

# Answer from the wiki

Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) when the question spans topics and you must verify a relationship link; [operations](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md) only if filing the answer is authorized — an unfiled answer opens no operation.
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

Question: $ARGUMENTS

Apply the [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium)
to the answer and any filed synthesis: keep Reddit-derived content under
`## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and Medium-derived content under
`## Medium articles`, even when retrieved through wiki summaries.

This mode does two things pure retrieval does not: it **synthesizes** an
answer (not just a list of matching pages) and it can **file that answer
back** into the wiki so the next question benefits from it. Retrieval itself
uses [search](search.md); use it for step 1 below rather than reimplementing
its search mechanics and health-disclosure logic here.

1. **Search**: read [search](search.md) and run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "..."` (add `--include-raw` if the question
   is plausibly about something recent enough that it may only exist as an
   unprocessed clipping, not yet a wiki/ page). Read the stderr status
   line(s) the search reference describes — **when the tier is not `hybrid`, or a
   raw/ check came back empty, say so in your answer.** A user reading a
   confident synthesis has no way to know the retrieval underneath it was
   degraded or incomplete.
2. Inspect result passages, scope, factual review dates and decision/backlog
   states (`search.mjs --json` exposes these). Read the canonical page, relevant
   alternatives and supporting evidence. A proposed ADR or planned feature is
   not current behavior. For cross-topic questions, follow explained relationship
   links and verify the inferred connection; do not mistake neighbors for evidence.
   Synthesize an answer that **cites** the pages/sources it rests on. A raw/
   hit (if `--include-raw` surfaced one) is unvetted evidence, not yet a
   reviewed claim — cite it as such, not as if it were an established
   wiki/ page. To verify a `wiki/` citation actually traces back to real
   evidence (rather than a broken or title-drifted link), pipe it into
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs"` — faster than opening the page
   and reading its `sources:` frontmatter by hand, and it reports a genuine
   gap plainly rather than you assuming the citation is good.
3. If filing is already authorized and the answer adds substantive knowledge,
   write or update the appropriate synthesis with provenance. Otherwise offer to
   file a substantive new answer and wait for acceptance; answering alone is
   read-only. Before creating or editing the page, open a query operation and
   retain the token. Validate citations, regenerate the catalog, log once, close
   the operation, and push and verify remote publication using the directly linked
   completion contract. Do not open an operation for an answer that is not filed.

# Search diagnostics and evidence routes

Use [search](search.md) for the ordinary read-only procedure. Load this reference
only when the detailed diagnostics or evidence route contracts are needed.

## How it works

`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "..."` runs a tiered lookup over `wiki/` and `moc/`:
The helper scans the Markdown files for keyword matches (exact phrase first, then all query terms, then partial matches) and needs no running app; a chunk-level semantic index
(built by `index-embed.mjs`, Ollama-backed) fuses in via Reciprocal Rank
Fusion when both a reachable Ollama and a built index are present. Results
print as `path:line` — the line is the passage that actually matched, so
read from there rather than the top of the page.

**A status line always prints to stderr. Read it, and tell the user when it
is not `hybrid`, and inspect channel failures even when it is.** Degradation can
leave plausible results with incomplete coverage; a fatal input/runtime error can
still fail. Report unavailable channels instead of interpreting no hits as no knowledge:
- `(hybrid · N chunks)` — keyword and chunk-level semantic, RRF-fused; channel status alone does not establish relevance. When the keyword scan finds the query exactly (1 to 3 pages hold the whole query as written, or a query of at most 5 terms has 1 to 3 pages holding every term in one paragraph), the semantic list stops voting in the final order, so an identifier or phrase is not displaced by topical neighbours; `--json` reports that as `semanticGate: { reason, pages }` (`null` when it did not apply). The tier is unchanged: semantic still admits candidates.
- `(lexical — <what is off> · run --health)` — keyword only. The
  results are still real, but semantic ranking contributed nothing. **Say so
  in your answer** — a user reading a confident result list has no way to
  know the retrieval was degraded.
- `(<tier> — keyword request failed (wiki) · run --health)` — a keyword scope failed. A failed `wiki/`
  scope (the primary one) drops the tier below `hybrid` even if `moc/` answered, so results come from the other
  channels only; **say so**. In `--json` output `channels` states each channel: `keyword.{wiki,moc,raw}` is `ok` or
  `failed`, `semantic` is `ok`, `failed`, `ollama-unavailable` or `index-unavailable`, and `identity` is `ok` or
  `incomplete`. A `raw/ clippings NOT searched` line means the raw scan failed: no raw hit is then not evidence of absence.

To diagnose: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" --health` for the full
report, `--setup` to display the exact remediation commands. Do not execute repairs during a read-only lookup. The usual causes are
Ollama not running, the embedding model not pulled, or the index not built
(`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-embed.mjs"`). Operational health is not relevance:
validate the returned page, status and supporting passage against the question.

For agent selection, use `--json --limit=10` to get bounded passages and metadata,
including project/type/status, factual review dates, provenance targets and index
freshness. Use `--project=<slug>`, `--type=<type>` or `--status=<state>` when the
question establishes a scope. Do not hide other domains when exploring complementary
ideas. Inspect decision/backlog state inside metadata before describing a proposal
as shipped. Exact titles and equivalent aliases are prioritized; ambiguous names
still require choosing the intended full path.

To list backlog items by their lifecycle, do not search for `status:`: that finds the
page status (`draft` or `maintained`). Run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-list.mjs" --project <slug> --backlog-status planned`
(also `--startable` and `--json`); [authoring](authoring.md) describes it.

**`op-commit` attempts an index refresh after every bracketed operation**; read
its notice for backend failures or a partial build. It cannot preempt edits outside
the operation — a hand edit in Obsidian, a `git pull` from
another machine. Hash-keyed vectors alone do not make a stale manifest current.
Search checks candidate file versions and reads passages from the current file;
modified semantic hits are excluded until refreshed and removed hits are dropped.
Read the per-result freshness and diagnostics; a live lexical/identity match can
still have an outdated embedding. `--health` reports changes since refresh.

## Explicit raw lookup

`wiki/` is the browsable, synthesized index; `raw/` is immutable clipped
evidence, deliberately excluded from both the keyword default and the
semantic index. The keyword scan can include raw evidence explicitly. **Pass `--include-raw`** to search both in one call:

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "your terms" --include-raw
```

Raw hits are appended after the normal `wiki/` result list (not blended into
the ranked/fused ordering — raw/ isn't chunked, so there is nothing to fuse
it against), and are self-evident by their `raw/...` path prefix. A
stderr line always discloses how many raw/ hits were found, including
`0` explicitly. Check raw-channel diagnostics too: an unavailable index with
zero returned hits does not establish that raw evidence is absent. **Reach for this before falling back to a
raw shell `rg`** — it uses the supported keyword scan and reports its coverage.

## Jumping from a wiki/ hit to its raw/ evidence

A `wiki/` hit is a synthesized page, not the evidence itself — normally,
reaching the raw clipping it rests on means opening the page and reading its
`sources:` frontmatter by hand. `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs"`
does that walk for you, and is built to take a hit straight from this
skill's own output, piped:

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "your terms" | node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs"
```

It also takes explicit paths (`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs"
"wiki/sources/Foo.md:23"` — the `:line` search.mjs prints is stripped
automatically), and a `raw/...` path passed straight through is reported as
already being the evidence, not re-resolved. It never guesses: a page whose
citation trail doesn't actually reach `raw/` is reported as `unreachable`
(a real gap — matches `health.mjs`'s `provenanceGaps`/`unreachableProvenance`
vocabulary) rather than silently omitted or invented, and a page that
legitimately has no provenance (`wiki/authored/`'s `sources: []`) is
reported as `declared-no-provenance`, distinctly — a deliberate disclosure,
not a defect.

# Find pages and passages

Resolve the plugin root from this skill's installed `SKILL.md`: two parents above
its containing folder. From this reference file, it is three parents above its
containing folder. Use quoted absolute helper paths, never workspace-relative
`scripts/` paths. The vault is `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT`, default `~/.wiki-master-vault`;
start at that known root and read applicable vault instructions. A configured
`WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` requires an explicit vault. Do not scan the user
profile or require a running Obsidian app.

1. Run a bounded search, replacing the path placeholder with the installed root:

   ```sh
   node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/search.mjs" "search terms" --json --limit=10
   ```

   The default scopes are `wiki/` and `moc/`. Add `--include-raw` explicitly for
   evidence lookup; raw is excluded by default. Use `--project=<slug>`,
   `--type=<type>` or `--status=<state>` only when the request establishes scope.
   For a different vault, set `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` for the command's scope and
   restore its prior value afterward; [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md#shell-portability)
   has shell-specific examples if needed.
2. Read stderr status and JSON `channels`, `diagnostics` and freshness metadata.
   Disclose non-`hybrid` search and failed channels even in a hybrid run. Lexical
   results are real, but semantic ranking contributed nothing. A failed primary
   `wiki/` scan means incomplete coverage; a failed raw scan means **not searched**,
   not zero evidence. Report the raw hit count when requested, including zero.
   Missing or stale indexes and zero hits never establish that the vault knows
   nothing. `search.mjs --health` reports coverage without repairing it.
3. Open the returned exact path at the matched line and read the surrounding
   passage. Exact titles and equivalent aliases are prioritized; disambiguate
   similarly named pages by full path and context. Inspect page status, review
   dates and decision/backlog state before describing a proposal as shipped.
   Healthy channels establish neither relevance nor factual support.
4. Return citation-ready paths and lines. For the raw source behind a wiki page,
   run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/resolve-evidence.mjs" "wiki/sources/Example.md:23"`.
   A citation route is not proof of a claim: before quoting or synthesizing, read
   [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) and verify the source.
   For a narrative answer use [query](query.md).

If a channel fails, use available results and bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/`
and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup and disclose missing
coverage. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`. Exclude dot folders, dependencies
and binary originals. Resolve paths within the known vault root.

This mode never writes content, opens operations, logs, commits or refreshes
indexes. Read [search details](search-details.md) only for ranking diagnostics,
evidence-route output, backlog listing or remediation guidance. Reporting a
degraded channel does not authorize running its repair commands.
